properties.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing
properties.description: Landing area of NASA's Perseverance rover in Jezero Crater.
properties.scienceReason: Provides the mission's reference location for exploring the crater floor, delta deposits and ancient lake environments.
properties.why: Useful as the starting point for the Jezero exploration map and route-planning demonstrations.
properties.survivalNote: Use local elevation and slope data; avoid assuming the landing ellipse is uniformly smooth.
properties.source: NASA Mars 2020 mission; coordinates used in project POI dataset.

properties.name: Perseverance Delta Exploration Waypoint
properties.description: A project waypoint representing Perseverance's exploration area near the western delta of Jezero Crater.
properties.scienceReason: The delta preserves sediment deposited where an ancient river entered a crater lake.
properties.why: Useful for highlighting the geological record of water transport and deposition.
properties.survivalNote: Delta terrain can include scarps, layered outcrops and loose sediment; inspect slope and imagery before routing.
properties.source: NASA Mars 2020 Jezero mission context; project waypoint coordinate.

properties.name: Belva Crater
properties.description: Impact crater feature identified in the team's Jezero-area map review.
properties.scienceReason: Crater interiors and ejecta can expose or redistribute geological materials, making them useful context for terrain interpretation.
properties.why: Adds a recognizable landform for map orientation and terrain-risk discussion.
properties.survivalNote: Crater rims and interior slopes may be steep; do not route across the rim without slope checks.
properties.source: Team map coordinate; feature interpretation should be checked against orbital imagery.

properties.name: Hartwell Crater
properties.description: Impact crater feature identified during the team's Jezero-area map review.
properties.scienceReason: Impact structures provide local relief and can expose subsurface materials.
properties.why: Useful as a terrain landmark and a candidate area for comparing crater-related hazards.
properties.survivalNote: Treat rim slopes and ejecta blocks as potential obstacles; coordinate is a map reading.
properties.source: Team map coordinate; verify against USGS Gazetteer/orbital imagery before operational use.

properties.name: Neretva Vallis
properties.description: One of the inlet valleys that fed the ancient Jezero lake and its western delta.
properties.scienceReason: Fluvial landforms and the associated delta record past water flow and sediment transport into Jezero.
properties.why: Important for reconstructing the ancient drainage and lake system.
properties.survivalNote: Valley walls and channel margins may be uneven or steep; this point is a regional marker, not a safe path.
properties.source: USGS planetary nomenclature; Jezero lake-system studies including https://doi.org/10.1029/2024JE008862.

properties.name: Una Vallis
properties.description: A valley name recorded from the team's Mars map review; exact feature identity and position need confirmation.
properties.scienceReason: If confirmed as a fluvial feature, it may help describe regional drainage and landscape evolution.
properties.why: Retain as a provisional map point pending confirmation from the official gazetteer or mapped imagery.
properties.survivalNote: Do not use as a routing destination until the feature and coordinate are verified.
properties.source: Team map reading; official feature record not yet confirmed.

properties.name: Sava Vallis
properties.description: One of the inlet valleys associated with the ancient Jezero lake and its eastern/western drainage system.
properties.scienceReason: Together with Neretva Vallis, it is evidence for water entering Jezero and building its delta deposits.
properties.why: Important for understanding the crater's ancient hydrology.
properties.survivalNote: Channel margins and valley walls may be steep; this is a regional science marker, not a traversable waypoint.

properties.name: Roubion Sample Site
properties.description: Perseverance's Roubion crater-floor sampling locality in the Máaz formation; the attempted core disaggregated during sampling.
properties.scienceReason: The site provides evidence about basaltic igneous rocks on the Jezero crater floor and the diversity of the Máaz formation.
properties.why: A published rover sampling location with a peer-reviewed coordinate.
properties.survivalNote: Rock fragments and uneven outcrop surfaces may impede travel; inspect high-resolution imagery and slope data.
properties.source: Simon et al. (2023), JGR: Planets, https://doi.org/10.1029/2022JE007474

properties.name: Rochette Sample Site
properties.description: Perseverance collected the Montdenier and Montagnac basalt cores at the Rochette outcrop.
properties.scienceReason: The basalt samples help characterize the igneous history and alteration of Jezero's crater-floor rocks.
properties.why: A published sample site useful for showing where rover science directly investigated crater-floor bedrock.
properties.survivalNote: Outcrop relief and scattered rocks can create local obstacles; use terrain layers before routing.
properties.source: Simon et al. (2023), JGR: Planets, https://doi.org/10.1029/2022JE007474

properties.name: Brac Sample Site
properties.description: Perseverance collected the Salette and Coulettes cores from the Brac outcrop in the Séítah formation.
properties.scienceReason: The samples are ultramafic cumulate rocks, providing evidence about the igneous composition and evolution of the crater floor.
properties.why: A peer-reviewed sampling location representing the Séítah geological unit.
properties.survivalNote: Layered and fractured outcrops may be rough; avoid steep or block-rich surfaces.
properties.source: Simon et al. (2023), JGR: Planets, https://doi.org/10.1029/2022JE007474

properties.name: Issole Sample Site
properties.description: Perseverance collected the Robine and Malay cores at the Issole outcrop near the mapped Séítah–Máaz boundary.
properties.scienceReason: The ultramafic samples help constrain the composition of the Séítah unit and its relationship to adjacent crater-floor materials.
properties.why: Useful for illustrating geological contacts and rover sampling strategy.
properties.survivalNote: Contact zones may have variable rock texture and relief; inspect local slope and imagery.
properties.source: Simon et al. (2023), JGR: Planets, https://doi.org/10.1029/2022JE007474

properties.name: Sid Sample Site
properties.description: Perseverance collected the Hahonih and Atsah cores at the Sid outcrop in the Máaz formation.
properties.scienceReason: The samples are described as andesitic igneous rocks and contribute to understanding the diversity of Jezero's crater-floor lithologies.
properties.why: A published rover sampling locality with direct scientific value.
properties.survivalNote: Rocky outcrops and loose surface material may complicate traversal; confirm the local hazard grid.
properties.source: Simon et al. (2023), JGR: Planets, https://doi.org/10.1029/2022JE007474

properties.name: Three Forks Sample Depot
properties.description: Perseverance's backup sample depot, where ten sample tubes were placed on the surface in a mapped zigzag pattern near the base of the ancient delta.
properties.scienceReason: The depot preserves a carefully documented collection of samples representing Jezero's geological history and is a key target for future sample-retrieval planning.
properties.why: A major mission landmark and scientifically important sample cache.
properties.survivalNote: NASA describes the depot ground as relatively flat, but local rocks, dust and approach conditions still require terrain checks.
properties.source: NASA/JPL-Caltech, https://science.nasa.gov/resource/perseverances-three-forks-sample-depot-map/; approximate map-derived centre, not an individual tube coordinate.

properties.name: Amalik Outcrop
properties.description: A named Perseverance investigation area associated with the western delta exploration; coordinate here is an approximate map placement.
properties.scienceReason: Outcrops in the delta region preserve sedimentary materials that can help reconstruct water flow, deposition and possible habitability.
properties.why: A useful science-interest marker, but its coordinate should be replaced with a rover traverse or image-derived position before routing.
properties.survivalNote: Outcrop surfaces may be layered, fractured or locally steep; do not treat this approximate point as a safe waypoint.
properties.source: Perseverance delta campaign literature; approximate coordinate requires verification against rover traverse data.

properties.name: Wildcat Ridge
properties.description: Perseverance investigated the Wildcat Ridge outcrop in the Shenandoah formation and collected the Hazeltop and Bearwallow samples.
properties.scienceReason: The sedimentary rocks are important for studying delta-related deposits and the preservation of possible biosignature-relevant materials.
properties.why: A scientifically significant sedimentary sampling locality; the coordinate here is only an approximate map placement.
properties.survivalNote: Layered sedimentary outcrops can have uneven surfaces and local scarps; verify exact rover coordinates before routing.
properties.source: NASA Mars 2020 sample inventory; https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20230000371/downloads/Herd_M2020_LPSC23_RSS_overview_final.pdf; approximate map placement.

properties.name: Marysville Crater
properties.description: An IAU-adopted impact crater in the broader Jezero study-region map extent.
properties.scienceReason: Impact craters provide stratigraphic context and can expose materials from beneath the surface.
properties.why: Officially named crater; the user's map reading (77.17°E, 18.13°N) is close to the USGS centre (77.18°E, 18.13°N).
properties.survivalNote: Crater rims and ejecta can be rough or steep; this site is outside the current elevation grid's southern boundary.

properties.name: Angelica Crater
properties.description: An IAU-adopted impact crater. The user's supplied coordinate (76.75°E, 18.64°N) is west of the official crater boundary.
properties.scienceReason: Impact structures provide geomorphic and stratigraphic context and may expose subsurface materials.
properties.why: Official centre is 76.95°E, 18.65°N; the user-provided point is not the crater centre and is retained in the coordinate note only.
properties.survivalNote: Crater rim terrain may be steep; this crater is west of the current elevation grid and should not be routed with that grid.

properties.name: Pliva Vallis
properties.description: The outlet valley on the eastern rim of Jezero Crater; USGS gives a centre location for the named linear feature.
properties.scienceReason: A 2025 study interprets the valley morphology as evidence for episodic lake-overflow events, with multiple incision episodes rather than one steady river.
properties.why: Important for reconstructing whether ancient Jezero operated as an open-basin lake and how its water system evolved.
properties.survivalNote: Valley walls, bedrock steps, dunes and layered deposits can create substantial hazards. The feature lies outside the current grid's eastern boundary; this point is a regional centre, not a safe route waypoint.
properties.source: USGS Gazetteer, Feature 15903: https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/15903; Le Deit et al. (2025), https://doi.org/10.1029/2024JE008862.
